chunks.text: Doc: MHD 01 (34482) WC July 2026 3 All dimensions in millimetres. FIG. 1 KOCHER PATTERN DISSECTOR 4 MATERIAL Stainless steel conforming to Designation X20Crl3 or X30Cr13 of IS 6603. 5 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 5.1 The dissector shall be free from burrs, pits, cracks, scales and other surface defects. 5.2 All edges including tip shall be even. 5.3 The dissector shall be polished bright and passivated. 6 HEAT TREATMENT The dissector shall be hardened and tempered to give a hardness of 400 to 460 HV. 7 TESTS 7.1 Rigidity Test Hold the dissector from the blade end in a suitable vice so that a length of 135 mm projects above the jaws. Apply a load of 170 N on the handle at a point 35 mm from its end. Attain the maximum load gradually and allow it to act for two minutes. On comple tion of the test the dissector shall not have acquired a permanent set. 7.2 Corrosion Resistance Test

chunks.title: Kocher Pattern Dissector — Specification

chunks.text: Doc: MHD 01 (34482) WC July 2026 4 The dissector shall satisfy the boiling and autoclaving test as mentioned in IS 7531. 7.2.1 Subject to agreement between the purchaser and the supplier, the dissect or may be put to the following test: 7.2.1.1 Copper Sulphate Test Scrub the sample with soap and warm water, rinse in shot water and then dip in 95 percent ethyl alcohol. Dry the sample. Immerse in copper sulphate solution at room temperature for 6 minutes and wash off with fresh water or swab with wet cotton wool. Composition of the solution shall be as follows: Copper sulphate (CuSO4.5H2O) 4.0 g Sulphuric acid (H2SO4) (sp gr 1.84) 10.0 g Reagent Water (see IS 1070) 90.0 ml No red stains or spots on the dissector shall be allowed but dulling of the polished surface may be permitted. 8 MARKING 8.1 Mark with the following: a) Manufacturer’s name, initials or his recognized trade-mark; and b) The words ‘Stainless Steel’. 8.2 BIS Certification Marking The product(s) confirming to the requirements of this standard may be certified as per the conformity assessment schemes under the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules and Regulations framed thereunder, and the product(s) may be marked with the Standard Mark. 9 PACKING Each dissector shall be wrapped in moisture -proof paper and put in a cardboard carton or shall be packed in a polyethylene bag. Dissectors m ay also be packed as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier.

chunks.source_file: MHD 1 (34489) WC_Surgical instruments - Corrosion resistance of stainless steel surgical instruments - Methods of tests (First Revision).pdf
chunks.text: Doc: MHD 01 (34489) WC July 2026 2 1 SCOPE This Indian Standard specifies the methods for testing of corrosion resistance of surgical instruments made from stainless steel. 2 REFERENCES The standards given below contain provisions which, through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision, and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of these standards. IS No. Title IS 1070 : 2023 Reagent Grade Water Specification (Fourth Revision) 3 TYPE OF TESTS 3.1 The following tests are specified for determining the corrosion resistance: a) Copper Sulphate Test b) Boiling Water Test c) Autoclaving Test 3.2 The purchaser shall specify whether all the tests are to be carried out, or if not, which of the tests are to be performed. If the purchaser does not so specify, it is left to the discretion of the manufacturer as to which test to apply. 4 COPPER SULPHATE TEST 4.1 Apparatus Glass or ceramic beaker. 4.2 Reagents 4.2.1 Copper (II) Sulphate Pentahydrate 4.2.2 Sulphuric Acid (rd 1.84) 4.2.3 Distilled Water Conforming to IS 1070. 4.3 Preparation of Test Solution Dissolve 4 g of copper sulphate ( 4.2.1) in 10 g of sulphuric acid ( 4.2.2). Cautiously, add the above to 90 ml of distilled water (see 4.2.3) taken in glass or ceramic beaker (4.1). 4.4 Preparation of Sample Scrub the surgical instrument using soap and water, rinse thoroughly in distilled water, dip in 95 percent (v/v) ethanol and dry. 4.5 Procedure

chunks.title: Surgical instruments - Corrosion resistance of stainless steel surgical instruments - Methods of tests (First Revision)
chunks.source_file: MHD 1 (34489) WC_Surgical instruments - Corrosion resistance of stainless steel surgical instruments - Methods of tests (First Revision).pdf
chunks.text: Doc: MHD 01 (34489) WC July 2026 3 4.5.1 Immerse the surgical instrument in the test solution ( 4.3) at room temperature for 6 min. Remove the instrument and wash it with distilled water or wipe it with wet cotton wool. Examine the instrument for evidence of deposition of copper. Except as specified under 4.5.1, there shall be no plating of copper on the instrument. 4.5.2 Slight deposit of copper on the periphery of the instrument, or at the soldered or brazed junctions or dulling of polished surfaces caused by copper sulphate solution shall be disregarded. Similarly, slight plating of copper in small parts of joints, ratchets and serrations shall be dis regarded. 5 BOILING WATER TEST 5.1 Reagent Distilled water conforming to IS 1070. 5.2 Apparatus Glass or ceramic beaker or suitable corrosion resistant stainless steel vessel. 5.3 Preparation of Sample Scrub the instrument using soap and warm water, rinse thoroughly in distilled water (5.1) and dry. 5.4 Procedure Immerse the instrument in boiling distilled water (see 5.1) in the beaker or vessel for at least 30 min. Subsequently allow the instrument to cool for at least 1 h in the water used for the test. Remove the instrument from the water and leave it exposed to the air for 2 h. 5.5 Rub the instrument vigorously with a dry cloth and examine it for the presence of blemishes or other signs of corrosion. Any blemish not removed by vigorous hand rubbing with a cloth shall be considered as evidence of corrosion. 6 AUTOCLAVING TEST 6.1 This test shall be performed subsequent to the boiling water test. 6.2 Autoclave A suitable autoclave of the non -vacuum type, with a minimum performance of 134°C and 200 KN/m2 (2.04kgf/cm2). 6.3 Water for Autoclaving Test It shall conform to IS 1070. 6.4 Procedure After cooling the instrument to room temperature following the boiling water test, place it unwrapped in a tray of the autoclave. Subject the instrument to six separate cycles of autoclaving each for 3 ± 1 2 minutes at a minimum temperature and pressure of 134ºC and 200 kN/m 2 (2.04 kgf/cm2) respectively. After each cycle, open the autoclave, remove the instrument and tray and allow it to cool to room temperature.

chunks.source_file: MHD 1 (34491) WC_Watson Cheyne Pattern Dissector — Specification.pdf
chunks.text: Doc: MHD 01 (34491) WC July 2026 3 5 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 5.1 The ends of the dissector shall be sharp as shown in Fig 1. 5.2 The dissector shall be free from pits, cracks, burrs and other surface flaws. 5.3 The dissector shall be polished bright and passivated. 6 HEAT TREATMENT The dissector shall be hardened and tempered to give a hardness of 380 to 430 HV. 7 TESTS 7.1 Flexibility Test 7.1.1 Hold the dissector in a vic at the middle so that its flat end points upwards and 86 mm of the shaft protrudes above the vice. Apply a force at the tip of the flat end, so as to deflect it in a plane at right angles to the long axis of the jaw of the vice by 7 mm as measured at the upper extremity of the flat end. On release of the force, no permanent set shall be observed. 7.1.2 Repeat the test with the dissector fixed at the middle of the shaft and the round end pointing upwards. Apply the force to the shaft at a point 86 mm above the upper surface of the vice in a plane at right angles to the long axis of the jaw of the vice. Deflect the shaft by 7 mm as measured at the level of the point where the force is applied. On release of the force, no permanent set shall be observed. 7.2 Corrosion Resistance Test Test the dissector in accordance with IS 7531. 8 MARKING 8.1 Each dissector shall be legibly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer’s initials or his recognized trade-mark. 8.2 BIS Certification Marking The product(s) confirming to the requirements of this standard may be certified as per the conformity assessment schemes under the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules and Regulations framed thereunder, and the product(s) may be marked with the Standard Mark. 9 PACKING As agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier.

FIG.1 MAYO PATTERN SCISSORS, DISSECTING, STRAIGHT AND CURVED ON FLAT 4 MATERIALS Scissors shall be made of stainless steel conforming to Designation X30Cr13 of IS 6603 or to the following composition: Element Percent Carbon 0.35 to 0.45 Silicon 0.10 to 0.70 Manganese 0.30 to 0.70 Nickel 1.00 Max Chromium 12.00 to 14.00 5 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 5.1 Scissors shall be symmetrical and well formed. 5.2 The blades along their length and the tips shall coincide and shall not over -ride, when the scissors are fully closed. 5.3 The blades shall open and close without stiffness and shall have a slight cross -over action to give a continuous pinch, and shall have no play at the joint. 5.4 Scissors shall be free from cracks, seams, burrs, flaws and other defects. The surfaces of the scissors shall be finished smooth, and polished bright passivated. The edges shall be even and rounded except for the cutting edge which shall be sharp. The cutting edge shall not have any feather, and shall be made hollow ground. 6 HARDNESS Scissors shall be evenly hardened and tempered to give a hardness of 550 to 650 HV.

chunks.source_file: MHD 10 (28479) WC_Medical Laboratory Instruments Vortex Mixer Specifications.pdf
chunks.text: Doc: MHD 10 (28479) WC September 2026 DRAFT FOR COMMENTS ONLY (Not to be reproduced without permission of BIS or used as an Indian Standard) भारतीय मानक मसौदा चिचकत्सा प्रयोगशाला हेतु उपकरण — भंवर चमश्रक — चवचशचि Draft Indian Standard Medical Laboratory Instruments – Vortex Mixer – Specifications ICS 71.040.20 Medical Laboratory Instruments Sectional Committee, MHD 10 Last date for comments: As per portal FOREWORD (Formal clauses will be added later) A vortex mixer is a laboratory device used to mix small vials of liquid. It consists of an electric motor with a vertically oriented drive shaft and a cupped piece mounted slightly off -centre. When the unit is turned on, the cupped piece oscillates rapidly, creating a vortex in the liquid. In medical laboratories, vortex mixers are essential for mixing reagents, suspending cells, or combining solutions for assays. They ensure thorough mixing, enhancing the accuracy and consistency of experiments and diagnostic tests. Their simplicity and effectiveness make them a staple in clinical research. A national standard for vortex mixers ensures uniformity in performance, safety, and quality across laboratories. This guarantees reliable and reproducible results, minimises equipment failure, and enhances user safety. Standardization also facilitates regulatory compliance and interoperability, promoting consistency in scientific research and diagnostic practices. To decide whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off per IS 2: 2022 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (second revision)’

chunks.text: Doc: MHD 10 (28479) WC September 2026 1 Draft Indian Standard Medical Laboratory Instruments – Vortex Mixer – Specification 1 Scope This Indian Standard specifies the requirements for electrically operated vortex mixers used in laboratories for mechanical mixing and stirring of small volumes of liquids. 2 Normative references The standards given below contain provisions which, through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision, and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of these standards. IS No. Title IS 17724 (Part 1):2023 Safety Requirements for Electrical Equipment for Measurement, Control, and Laboratory Use Part 1 General Requirements (IEC 61010 -1: 2010 + AMD1:2016 + COR1:2019, MOD) IS 15575 (Part 1) : 2016 IEC 61672-1 : 2013 Electroacoustics - Sound Level Meters 3 Terms and definitions For the purposes of this standard, the following terms and definitions apply. 3.1 Base Unit Main body of the vortex mixer containing the drive mechanism, motor, control system, and supporting structure. 3.2 Cup Head Interchangeable resilient attachment mounted on the drive mechanism that supports the sample container during mixing. 3.3 Platform Attachment Interchangeable accessory used for simultaneous mixing of multiple sample containers or microplates. 3.4 Orbit Diameter of the circular path described by the centre of the cup head or platform during operation.

chunks.text: Doc: MHD 10 (28479) WC September 2026 2 3.5 Mixing Speed Rotational or oscillatory operating speed of the drive mechanism, expressed in revolutions per minute (rpm). 3.6 Maximum Sample Capacity Maximum mass, volume, or number of sample containers that the vortex mixer is designed to operate simultaneously, as declared by the manufacturer. 3.7 Stability Ability of the vortex mixer to remain stationary without tipping, sliding, or excessive movement during operation under specified conditions. 3.8 Mixing Efficiency Ability of the vortex mixer to produce a homogeneous mixture within a specified time under prescribed test conditions. 3.9 Duty Cycle Specified period of operation and rest during which the vortex mixer is intended to operate without exceeding its design limits. 4 General Requirements 4.1 General 4.1.1 The vortex mixer shall be designed and constructed to operate safely and reliably under the environmental and operating conditions specified by the manufacturer. 4.1.2 The instrument shall comply with the applicable safety requirements specified in IS 17724 (Part 1). 4.2 Construction 4.2.1 The vortex mixer shall be of robust construction and shall be free from defects that may affect its performance, safety, or service life. 4.2.2 All components shall be securely assembled and shall withstand the mechanical stresses encountered during normal operation. 4.2.3 The rotating assembly shall be securely attached to prevent loosening or detachment during operation. 4.3 Materials 4.3.1 Materials used for the external housing and components exposed to laboratory reagents shall be resistant to corrosion, cleaning agents, and commonly encountered laboratory chemicals. 4.3.2 Materials shall not exhibit cracking, swelling, deformation, or deterioration under normal conditions of use. 4.4 Stability 4.4.1 The vortex mixer shall remain stable throughout its operation. There shall be no tipping, no detachment of components, and no movement sufficient to impair safe operation or intended performance.

chunks.text: Doc: MHD 10 (28479) WC September 2026 3 4.5 Controls 4.5.1 The operating controls shall be clearly identified and easily accessible. 4.5.2 Adjustment of operating parameters shall not result in unsafe operation. 4.5.3 Where provided, the direction of adjustment shall be clearly indicated. 4.6 Operating Modes 4.6.1The vortex mixer shall provide touch operation, continuous operation, or both, as declared by the manufacturer. 4.7 Accessory Mounting 4.7.1 Cup heads, platform attachments, and other accessories supplied by the manufacturer shall be securely fitted and shall not become detached during operation. 4.8 Electrical Supply 4.8.1 The rated voltage, frequency, and rated input shall be declared by the manufacturer. 4.9 Protection Against Overheating 4.9.1 The vortex mixer shall comply with the applicable requirements for equipment temperature limits and resistance to heat specified in Clause 10 of IS 17724 (Part 1). 4.10 Finish 4.10.1 Metallic parts shall be adequately protected against corrosion. 4.10.2 The external finish shall withstand normal laboratory cleaning and handling without deterioration. 4.11 Noise and Vibration 4.11.1 The instrument shall operate without abnormal vibration, excessive noise, or mechanical instability. 5. Construction requirements 5.1 Housing The housing shall enclose the internal components necessary for safe operation and shall provide protection against access to hazardous parts and mechanical damage during normal use. 5.2 Drive Mechanism The drive mechanism shall produce the declared orbital motion without abnormal vibration or mechanical interference. 5.3 Accessories Cup heads and platform attachments shall fit securely and be readily removable without damage. 5.4 Control System The speed control shall permit adjustment of the mixing speed throughout the declared operating range without interruption of operation or unintended stopping.

Safety requirements 7.1 Electrical safety shall comply with IS 17724 (Part 1). 7.2 Protective earthing where applicable, shall comply with IS 17724 (Part 1). 7.3 Moving parts shall not present mechanical hazards during normal operation. 8 Testing requirements 8.1 Visual Examination 8.1.1 The vortex mixer shall be visually examined for compliance with the requirements specified in Clauses 4.2, 4.3, 4.5, 4.7 and 4.10. 8.1.2 The examination shall include verification of: a) workmanship, b) finish, c) assembly of components, d) identification of controls, e) accessory mounting and f) visible defects. 8.1.3 The vortex mixer shall comply with the applicable requirements specified in Clauses 4.2, 4.3, 4.5, 4.7. 8.1.4 Compliance with 4.10.1 shall be verified by visual examination. The exposed metallic parts shall be free from visible corrosion, flaking or deterioration that may affect the safety or intended performance of the vortex mixer. 8.1.5 Compliance with 5.1 shall be verified by visual examination and by the applicable enclosure and mechanical strength tests specified in IS 17724 (Part 1). 8.2 Speed Accuracy Test 8.2.1 Apparatus

chunks.text: Doc: MHD 10 (28479) WC September 2026 5 A calibrated non-contact tachometer having an accuracy of ±0.5 percent or more. 8.2.2 Procedure The speed of the vortex mixer shall be measured at the minimum, intermediate and maximum settings declared by the manufacturer. The measured speed shall be recorded after steady operation has been achieved. 8.2.3 Acceptance Criteria The measured speed shall comply with the requirements specified in 6.1. 8.3 Orbit Diameter Measurement 8.3.1 Apparatus Suitable measuring instrument having a least count of 0.1 mm. 8.3.2 Procedure The orbit diameter shall be measured as the diameter of the circular path described by the centre of the cup head during operation. 8.3.3 Acceptance Criteria The measured orbit diameter shall comply with the requirements specified in 6.2. 8.4 Stability Test 8.4.1 Procedure a) The vortex mixer shall be placed on a rigid, horizontal surface, b) The standard cup head shall be fitted, c) The mixer shall be operated in the continuous mode at the maximum declared speed for 30 min, d) The instrument shall be observed throughout the test. 8.4.2 Acceptance Criteria During and after completion of the test, a) the vortex mixer shall not tip over, b) no component shall become detached, c) no movement shall occur that impairs safe operation and d) the vortex mixer shall remain functional. 8.5 Mixing Performance Test 8.5.1 Apparatus a) 50 ml centrifuge tube, b) distilled water, c) aqueous dye solution.

chunks.text: Doc: MHD 10 (28479) WC September 2026 6 8.5.2 Procedure a) Fill the centrifuge tube with 50 ml of distilled water. b) Add 0.5 ml of dye solution. c) Operate the vortex mixer at the maximum declared speed for 10 s. d) Visually examine the contents immediately after mixing. 8.5.3 Acceptance Criteria No visible streaks, sediment, or unmixed regions shall be observed. 8.6 Temperature Rise Test 8.6.1 The temperature rise of the vortex mixer shall be determined in accordance with the applicable requirements specified in IS 17724 (Part 1). 8.6.2 The measured temperature rise shall comply with the requirements specified in IS 17724 (Part 1). 8.7 Noise Measurement 8.7.1 Apparatus A sound level meter conforming to class 2 as specified in IS 15575 (Part 1). 8.7.2 Procedure The sound pressure level shall be measured at a distance of 1 m from the vortex mixer while operating at the maximum declared speed. 8.7.3 Acceptance Criteria The measured sound pressure level shall comply with the requirements specified in Clause 6.5. 8.8 Endurance Test 8.8.1 Procedure The vortex mixer shall be operated continuously at the maximum declared speed for 8 h under no - load conditions. Following completion of the test, the instrument shall be visually examined and operated. 8.8.2 Acceptance Criteria After completion of the test, a) the vortex mixer shall remain functional, b) no component shall become loose or detached, c) no abnormal vibration or noise shall be observed and d) the vortex mixer shall comply with the applicable performance requirements specified in 6.

chunks.text: Doc: MHD 12 (34150) WC July 2026 3 6 CONSTRUCTION REQUIREMENTS 6.1 Framework The examination table shall have a framework of single continuous lengths of mild steel tubes as shown in Fig. 1. chunks.text: Doc: MHD 12 (34151) WC July 2026 1 1 SCOPE This standard specifies the construction and performance requirements for manually controlled hydraulic operation tables. 2 REFERENCES The standards given below contain provisions which, through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision, and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of these standards. IS No. Title IS 1300: 1994 Phenolic moulding materials - Specification (third revision) IS 6911: 2017 Stainless steel plate, sheet and strip - Specification ( second revision) IS 1068: 2025 ISO 1456: 2009 Metallic and other inorganic coatings - Electrodeposited coatings of nickel, nickel plus chromium, copper plus nickel and of copper plus nickel plus chromium (fourth revision) IS 17523: 2021 Castors and Wheels - Requirements for Castors for Furniture 3 TERMINOLOGY 3.1 Operation Table - The surgical operation table is fitted with a hydraulic pump to raise and lower the table top with a head -end control for positioning of the table top during surgical operations. 3.2 Jerk - The sudden change in speed or quick movement. 4 MATERIAL REQUIREMENTS 4.1 The materials used in the manufacture of the operation table shall be corrosion-resistant or protective finished. 4.2 The raising column and the gearing system shall be made from materials to resist wear during normal manipulation. 4.3 The handles provided shall be made from ebonite or plastics as per Grades 1 or 2 of IS 1300. 4.4 The stainless steel used shall conform to designation X04Cr18Ni10 or X07Cr17Ni12Mo2 in accordance with IS 6911. 4.5 The operation table shall have an antistatic rubber tread castor as per IS 17523 or cotton impregnated Bakelite wheels. The operation table shall have a static charge transmission mechanism to the earth. 5 SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS 5.1 Table Top The minimum overall length of the table top shall be 180 cm with the head section and 195 cm without the head section. The overall width of the table top excluding side railings shall be 50 to 55 cm. 5.2 Height The height of the table top without mattress shall be 75± 7.5 cm and in th e extreme lifted position 115±5 cm subject to limitation of the hydraulic lift as specified in 6.4.

chunks.title: Hydraulic Operation Table - Specification (First Revision)
chunks.source_file: MHD 12 (34151) WC_Hydraulic Operation Table - Specification (First Revision).pdf
chunks.text: Doc: MHD 12 (34151) WC July 2026 2 6 CONSTRUCTION REQUIREMENTS 6.1 Design A typical design for the operation table shall be as per Fig. 1. Fig. 1 HYDRAULIC MAJOR OPERATION TABLES 6.2 Base The base shall be solid and mounted on castors to provide stability to the operation table. The base shall have non-skid compensating floor locks actuated by a foot pedal. The base may also have foot rails for providing a comfortable footrest for the surgical team. 6.3 Table Top The table top shall have a minimum of four sections namely, head, trunk (two sections) and leg sections. The head section shall be detachable. The detachable feature for the leg section depends on manufacturer and purchaser requirements. The entire table top shall have a jerk - free vertical movement. The multiple cylinder hydraulic systems may have sudden change in speed (jerk) as a result of cylinder diameter differences which shall not be in excess of ‘n —1’, where ‘n’ is the number of cylinders. The minor operation table shall also satisfy the following requirements: a) The entire table top shall be capable of being tilted to 45 °±3° in Trendelenburg and reverse Trendelenburg positions. b) The table shall have arrangements for a lateral tilt of 20°±2° in either direction. c) The table shall allow angulation in flex (90 °) and reflex (220 °) positions in one or several cranking operations (see Fig. 2). d) The table top may be provided with a perineal cut-out for the drainage tray. e) The table top shall have a separate kidney elevator if there is no specific arrangement to obtain kidney position which is capable of raising at 150 mm from the table top and shall have a head-end control for manipulation. f) The entire table top shall have a sweep of 360° in the horizontal plane as required by the purchaser. 6.3.1 Head and Leg Sections

chunks.title: Hydraulic Operation Table - Specification (First Revision)
chunks.source_file: MHD 12 (34151) WC_Hydraulic Operation Table - Specification (First Revision).pdf
chunks.text: Doc: MHD 12 (34151) WC July 2026 3 The head section shall be able to raise 40° to 45° and in its reverse position 120° from the trunk portion. The head section shall be so designed to be attached on the leg section side in the sitting position. The leg section shall be capable of being raised or lowered to 90° from the trunk so as to enable the table to be used as a chair. The locking mechanism shall be provided at stages of every 15° angle in the sitting position to prevent wobbling of the foot section. The head section and the table top shall have controls capable of positioning during operation and which shall not interfere with the surgical team. The controls are situated on the head-end side and the various controls may be independent or at one single control point actuated through a gear mechanism with an indicator dial shall be controlled by a common crank or wheel with folding handles. 6.4 Hydraulic Lift The table shall have a hydraulic pump encased in the base for controlling the lift of the table. The hydraulic pump shall be operated by a pedal. The table lift shall be between 30 to 50 cm. 7 ACCESSORIES 7.1 The Table 1 shall be provided with the following standard accessories: Table 1 List of Accessories Sr. No. Accessories Count in (No.) 1 Foot extension 1 2 Shoulder supports 2 3 Lateral supports or side supports 2 4 Anaesthetic screen 1 5 Kidney elevator 1 6 Arms support 1 7 Pelvic holder strap 1 8 Leg strap 2 9 Wristlets 2 10 Pair of knee crutches/lithotomy leg holders 2 11 Intravenous arm board 1

chunks.text: Doc: MHD 12 (34151) WC July 2026 6 8 PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS 8.1 Hydraulic Lift The hydraulic lift shall give a vertical jerk-free and smooth movement to the system as per 6.3. When the hydraulic pressure is released, the table top shall take travel time of 15 seconds to 45 seconds from the maximum height to the bottom most position. The downward movement shall be smooth and jerk-free as per 6.3. When the table top is held in any position by hydraulic action alone and loaded with 150 kg in the trunk portion the height shall not reduce more than 3 mm in a period of four hours. Fig. 5 REFLEX AND FLEX POSITIONS 8.2 Base The base shall be stable on the castors with non -skid floor lock s. The table shall be applied with 12 kg load to move the table on a smooth cemented floor, once the table shall come in motion the 7 kg load shall be sufficient for the motion. The floor locks shall give rigidity to the table and the table shall not move in any direction when a force of 50 kg is applied to the base in any direction. 8.3 Table Top The table top shall satisfy the requirements given below in any position obtained by the hydraulic lift: a) The extreme edge of the head section shall be applied with a vertical load of 50 kg, when the load is applied the leg section shall not lift by more than 10 mm.

chunks.text: Doc: MHD 12 (34151) WC July 2026 7 b) The extreme end of the head section (with the head section drawn in) shall be applied with a load of 5 kg which is dropped from a height of 150 mm, when the load is applied the head section shall not fold in. c) The head section shall be pulled along its plane with a load of 25 kg, when the load is applied the head section shall not come off when locked. d) There shall be no wobble under normal working conditions when the accessories are clamped. 9 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 9.1 The operation table components shall be arranged accurately to give smooth operation and additional performance requirements provided in 8. The operation table surfaces shall be well finished and free from surface defects, such as pinholes, blisters, blow-holes and similar other defects. The edges shall be rounded off and the four sections comprising the table top in their normal position shall be in one plane when tested with a spirit level. The sweeps of the head and leg sections shall be true. The welded joints shall have welds fully penetrating and well finished. The operation table metal surfaces shall be non -corrosive (aluminium and sta inless steel) with matt finish. 9.2 The corrosive surface like steel castings for base, cylinder casings, foot pedals shall be painted to shades such as sea green or low reflective shades agreed to between the manufacturer and the purchaser. Initially the surface which is painted shall be de greased, rust-proofed by phosphating and then suitably protected by an anti-corrosive primer with brushing or spraying and then finished by spraying in stove enamel or air -drying enamel of the specified shade. During the procedure each stage shall be separately stoved or air-dried. 9.3 The resulting finish shall be hard and shall not readily chip or flake. The mild steel and brass parts shall be plated chromium over nickel according to Service Condition 2 of IS 1068. 10 MARKING 10.1 The marking which is used by the manufacturer shall be legibly and indelibly marked with the Identification mark of the manufacturer. 10.2 Each operation table shall have a name plate fixed to it showing the following: a) Range of hydraulic lift; b) Any special instructions for safe handling of the table. 10.3 BIS Certification Marking The product(s) conforming to the requirements of this standard may be

chunks.text: Doc: MHD 12 (34160) WC July 2026 1 1 SCOPE This standard specifies the construction and performance requirements for manually controlled height minor operation hydraulic tables. 2 REFERENCES The standards given below contain provisions which, through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision, and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of these standards. IS No. Title IS 6911: 2026 Stainless Steel Plate, Sheet and Strip - Specification (third revision) IS 1068: 2025 ISO 1456: 2009 Metallic and other inorganic coatings - Electrodeposited coatings of nickel, nickel plus chromium, copper plus nickel and of copper plus nickel plus chromium (fourth revision) IS 17523: 2021 Castors and Wheels - Requirements for Castors for Furniture 3 TERMINOLOGY 3.1 Minor Operation Table - A surgical operation table fitted with a hydraulic pump or mechanical device (or electro-mechanical device) to raise and lower. 3.2 Jerk - The sudden change in speed or quick movement. 4 MATERIAL REQUIREMENTS 4.1 The materials used in the manufacture of the minor operation table shall be corrosion - resistant or protective finished. 4.2 The raising column and the gearing system shall be made from materials to resist wear during normal manipulation. 4.3 The handles provided shall be made from ebonite or phenol formaldehyde. 4.4 The stainless steel used shall conform to designation X07Cr17Ni12Mo2 in accordance with IS 6911. 4.5 The minor operation table shall have an antistatic rubber tread or stainless steel castor as per IS 17523. The operation table shall have a static charge transmission mechanism to the earth. 5 SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS 5.1 Table Top The overall length of the table top shall be 180±5 cm with the head section and 195±5 cm without the head section. The overall width of the table top excluding side railings shall be 50 to 55 cm. 5.2 Height The height of the table top without mattress shall be 80±5 cm and in the extreme lifted position preferably between 95±5 cm subject to limitation of the hydraulic lift as specified in 6.4. 6 CONSTRUCTION REQUIREMENTS 6.1 Design A typical design for the minor operation table shall be as per Fig. 1.

chunks.text: Doc: MHD 12 (34160) WC July 2026 2 Fig. 1 MINOR OPERATION HYDRAULIC TABLES 6.2 Base The base shall be solid and mounted on castors to provide stability to the minor operation table. The base shall have non-skid compensating floor locks actuated by a foot pedal. The base may also have foot rails for providing a comfortable footrest for the surgical team. 6.3 Table Top The table top shall have a minimum of three sections, namely, head, trunk and leg sections. The head section shall be detachable. The detachable feature for the leg section depends on manufacturer and purchaser requirements. The entire table top shall have a jerk -free vertical movement. The multiple cylinder hydraulic systems may have sudden change in speed (jerk) as a result of cylinder diameter differences which shall not be in excess of ‘n —1’, where ‘n’ is the number of cylinders. The minor operation table shall also satisfy the following requirements: a) The entire table top shall be capable of being tilted to 30 °±1° in Trendelenburg and reverse Trendelenburg positions. b) The table shall have arrangements for a lateral tilt of 20°±2° in either direction. c) The table top may be provided with a perineal cut-out for the drainage tray. 6.3.1 Head and Leg Sections The head section shall be able to raise 40° to 45° and in its reverse position 90° from the trunk portion. The leg section shall be capable of being raised or lowered to 90° from the trunk to enable the table to be used as a chair. The head section and the table top shall have controls capable of positioning during operation and the controls shall be situated so as not to interfere with the surgical team. The various controls may be independent and on sides of the table with removable type or folding type handles. 6.4 Hydraulic Lift The table shall have a hydraulic pump or mechanical device (or electro -mechanical device) lifting/lowering device fitted with the base of the table. The table shall operate by a paddle or a handle. The table lift shall be between 15 to 25 cm. The controls shall have easy access and various component parts of the controls and the table shall be easy to clean and maintain. All parts intended to be removed by the user shall be easy to replace with parts of the same make and difficult to assemble

chunks.text: Doc: MHD 12 (34160) WC July 2026 3 7 ACCESSORIES 7.1 The Table 1 shall be provided with the following standard accessories: Table 1 List of Accessories Sr. No. Accessories 1 Foot extension 2 Shoulder supports, Side supports with antistatic rubber pads 3 Anaesthetic screen 4 Leather Wristlets 5 Pair of knee crutches/lithotomy leg holders 6 25 to 50 mm thick antistatic foam rubber mattress NOTE - When antistatic rubber is not used, the construction of the table shall ensure transmission of static charge to the earth. 8 PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS 8.1 Hydraulic Lift The hydraulic lift shall give a vertical jerk-free and smooth movement to the system. When the hydraulic pressure is released, the table top shall take not less than 10 seconds and not more than 30 seconds to travel from the maximum height to the bottom most position. The downward movement shall be smooth and subject to limitations in 6.3. When the table top is held in any position by hydraulic action alone, and loaded with 150 kg in the trunk portion, it shall not sink by more than 3 mm in a period of four hours. 8.2 Base The base shall be stable on the castors with non -skid floor lock s. The table shall be applied with 120N load to move the table on a smooth cemented floor after the table is moved 70N the load shall be sufficient for the motion. The floor locks shall give rigidity to the table and the table shall not move in any direction when a force of 500N is applied to the base in any direction. 8.3 Table Top The table top shall satisfy the requirements given below in any position obtained by the hydraulic lift: a) The extreme edge of the head section shall be applied with a vertical load of 500N, when the load is applied the leg section shall not lift by more than 15 mm. b) The extreme end of the head section (with the head section drawn in) shall be applied with a load of 5 kg which is dropped from a height of 150 mm, when the load is applied the head section shall not get detached. c) The head section shall be pulled along its plane with a load of 250N, when the head section is locked it shall not come off. d) There shall be no wobble under normal working conditions

chunks.text: Doc: MHD 12 (34160) WC July 2026 4 9 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 9.1 The minor operation table components shall provide smooth operation and additional performance requirements as per 8. The operation table surfaces shall be well finished and free from surface defects, such as pinholes, blisters, blow-holes and similar other defects. The edges shall be rounded off and the three sections comprising the table top in their normal position shall be in one plane when tested with a spirit level. The sweeps of the head and leg sections shall be easy. The welded joints shall have welds fully penetrating and well finished. The minor operation table metal surfaces shall be non-corrosive (aluminium and stainless steel) with matt finish. 9.2 The corrosive surface like steel castings for base, cylinder casings, foot pedals shall be painted to shades such as sea green or low reflective shades agreed to between the manufacturer and the purchaser. Initially the surface which is painted shall be de greased, rust-proofed by phosphating and then suitably protected by an anti-corrosive primer with brushing or spraying and then finished by spraying in stove enamel or air -drying enamel of the specified shade. During the procedure each stage shall be separately stoved or air-dried. 9.3 The resulting finish shall be hard and shall not readily chip or flake. The mild steel and brass parts shall be plated chromium over nickel according to Service Condition 2 of IS 1068. 10 MARKING 10.1 The marking which is used by the manufacturer shall be legibly and indelibly marked with the Identification mark of the manufacturer. 10.2 Each minor operation table shall have a name plate fixed to it showing the following: a) Range of hydraulic lift; b) Any special instructions for safe handling of the table. 10.3 BIS Certification Marking The product(s) conforming to the requirements of this standard may be certified as per the conformity assessment schemes under the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules and Regulations framed thereunder, and the product(s) may be marked with the Standard Mark. 11 OPERATING MANUAL 11.1 The minor operation table shall be accompanied by instructions manual giving the following information: a) Brief instructions for installation and maintenance (including spare parts), and b) Instructions for correct operation of the table. 12 PACKAGING The minor operation table shall be packed as agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer. All standards are subject to revision, and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of these standards. 3 MATERIAL REQUIREMENTS 3.1 Framework The material used for the framework shall be as per 3.1 of IS 4033. 3.2 Shelves The shelves used in the medicine trolley shall be made from materials specified in 3.2 (a) to 3.2 (c) of IS 4033. 3.3 Railings The railings used in the medicine trolley shall be made from mild steel strips in accordance with IS 513 (Part 2) or IS 1029 or mild steel tube of 15 mm diameter as per IS 1239 (Part 1). 3.4 Domed Caps The domed caps used for closing the framework tubing which shall be made up of mild steel or aluminium or PVC. 3.5 Bowls The bowls used in medicine trolleys shall be made from stainless steel conforming to designation X07Cr18Ni9 of IS 6911. 4 SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS The shape and dimensions of the medicine trolley shall be as given in Fig. 1. Tolerance on all dimensions ±5 mm All dimensions in millimetres Fig. 1 MEDICINE TROLLEY

chunks.title: Medicine Trolley - Specification (First Revision)
chunks.source_file: MHD 12 (34164) WC_Medicine Trolley - Specification (First Revision).pdf
chunks.text: Doc: MHD 12 (34164) WC July 2026 2 5 CONSTRUCTION REQUIREMENTS 5.1 The medicine trolley shall have a welded framework of continuous lengths of mild steel tube as shown in Fig. 1. 5.2 The shelves and the railings used in the medicine trolley shall be welded to the upright members. 5.3 The upper ends of the upright members shall be fitted with domed caps. 5.4 The medicine trolley shall be fitted with castors conforming to IS 17523. 5.4.1 The wheels of the castors shall have antistatic rubber tread or alternatively the construction of the medicine trolley shall be such as to ensure transmission of static charge to the earth. 5.5 The medicine trolley shall be provided with two stainless steel bowls which shall rest on rings hinged to the upright members as per Fig. 1. 6 TESTING REQUIREMENTS 6.1 Adhesion Test The adhesion test required for the medicine trolley shall conform to 6.1.1 of IS 4033. 6.2 Performance Test The performance test for the medicine trolley shall be as per 6.1.2 of IS 4033 which is tested by putting additional load. 6.2.1 The performance test shall be carried out and it is noted that the shelves shall not get displaced or make rattling noise. 7 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 7.1 The medicine trolley shall be free from cracks, sharp edges and burrs. 7.2 The finish for the medicine trolley shall be in accordance with 7 of IS 4033. The enamels for the undercoating and finishing coat shall conform to IS 2932. 8 MARKING 8.1 The marking which is used by the manufacturer shall be legibly and indelibly marked with the Identification mark of the manufacturer. 8.2 BIS Certification Marking The product(s) conforming to the requirements of this standard may be certified as per the conformity assessment schemes under the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules and Regulations framed thereunder, and the product(s) may be marked with the Standard Mark. 9 PACKAGING The medicine trolley shall be packed as agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer. Each individual package shall contain only one unit and may be marked with the name of the item, and identification of the source of manufacture and batch number and any other marking if so desired.

chunks.text: Doc: MHD 12 (34166) WC July 2026 1 1 SCOPE This standard specifies the dimensional and other requirements for Silverman type liver biopsy needle. 2 REFERENCES The standards given below contain provisions, which, through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision, and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of these standards. IS No. Title IS 6911: 2026 Stainless Steel Plate, Sheet and Strip - Specification ( third revision) IS 17964 (Part 7): 2025 Small-bore connectors for liquids and gases in healthcare applications: Part 7 Connectors for intravascular or hypodermic applications IS 1068 : 2025/ ISO 1456 : 2009 Metallic and other inorganic coatings — Electrodeposited coatings of nickel, nickel plus chromium, copper plus nickel and of copper plus nickel plus chromium ( fourth revision ) IS 4905: 2015 ISO 24153: 2009 Random sampling and randomization procedures (first revision) 3 TERMINOLOGY 3.1 Lug - The small projection on the Luer connector of specialized needles to indicate the bevel's orientation. 3.2 Luer Connector - The tapered fitting that creates a leak -free, secure and detachable connection. 3.3 Stilette - It is a thin, solid rod that is inserted into a hollow medical needle (cannula). 3.4 Adopter - The adopter is a device used to securely connect a needle to another component, such as a syringe, IV tubing or blood collection tube holder. 3.5 Cannula - The cannula is a tube that can be inserted into the body, often for the delivery or removal of fluid or for the gathering of samples. 4 MATERIAL REQUIREMENTS 4.1 The cannula shall be made from stainless steel drawn tubing which conform to designation X07Cr18Ni9S or X04Cr17Ni12Mo2 of IS 6911. 4.2 The Luer Connector materials requirements shall be as per Annex G of IS 17964 (Part 7). 4.3 The stilette wire shall be made from stainless steel wire.

The cannula and the Luer connector shall be concentric and well aligned.

chunks.text: Doc: MHD 12 (34166) WC July 2026 3 6.3 The puncture and biopsy needle shall be sharpened on three aspects as shown in Fig. 1. The points on both the needles shall be well defined and free from any feather edge, irregularity and burrs when examined under 10X to 15X magnification. 7 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 7.1 Workmanship 7.1.1 The cannula shall be smooth both outside and inside and free from pits, cracks, tool marks, burrs, embedded foreign matter and other surface defects. 7.1.2 The stilette wire shall be smooth, bright and free from foreign matter and shall slide smoothly into the cannula. 7.2 Finish The Luer connector shall be free from pits, burrs, cracks, sharp edges, tool marks, roughness and other surface defects. It shall be plated both inside and outside chromium over nickel conforming to 5.6 of IS 1068 and polished. The plating shall be such as to withstand the corrosion test given at 6.5 of IS 1068. 8 TESTING REQUIREMENTS 8.1 Leakage Test for Puncture Needle The needle shall be fit to a tested syringe and connect the syringe to a source of water on which pressure could be applied. The water through the needle point shall be started and sealed by piercing into a piece of solid rubber and applying a pressure of 3 Bar for 10 seconds. No leakage shall be observed at the joint of the Luer connector and the syringe or the cannula and the Luer connector. 8.2 Sharpness of Puncture Needle Point The aluminium foil of 0.02±0.01 mm thickness is cleaned with alcohol or benzene and mounted suitably so that it is spread taut and the needle may penetrate vertically. The needle shall be kept vertically with its point touching the foil and ensuring that the weight of the needle did not act on the foil. Then the load on the Luer connector shall be gently started with one gram. The load on foil shall be increased gradually till 30 seconds. The needle shall penetrate the aluminium foil with a test load less than 30±0.5 g. 8.3 Flexibility of Biopsy Needle The split portions of the biopsy needle shall be pulled so that the tips separate by 30 mm and released. This shall be done 5 times. The needle shall not break or take a permanent set. 8.4 Security of Swaging The swaging of the cannula of the puncture needle with the Luer

The needle shall penetrate the aluminium foil with a test load less than 30±0.5 g. 8.3 Flexibility of Biopsy Needle The split portions of the biopsy needle shall be pulled so that the tips separate by 30 mm and released. This shall be done 5 times. The needle shall not break or take a permanent set. 8.4 Security of Swaging The swaging of the cannula of the puncture needle with the Luer connector shall be tested by applying a pull of 9 kg for one minute. The cannula shall not come out of the Luer connector and it shall not become loose. 8.5 Corrosion Resistance The complete needle shall be immersed in a 10 percent solution of citric acid at room temperature for 5 hours. It shall then be boiled in distilled water for 30 minutes and cooled while immersed in the same for 48 hours. The cannula or Luer connector shall show no corrosion. The test shall be conducted in a glass container. 8.6 Freedom from Foreign Matter The cannula and the Luer connector shall be examined under good illumination with a magnifying lens, they shall be free from foreign matter, metal particles or chips, pits, burrs and other defects. 9 SAMPLING PROCEDURE The Sampling procedure and criteria for conformity for liver biopsy needle may be as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. chunks.text: Doc: MHD 12 (34169) WC July 2026 3 6 CONSTRUCTION REQUIREMENTS 6.1 Framework The obstetric labour table shall have a welded framework of continuous lengths of angle iron of size 40 mm × 40 mm × 3 mm. The four upright members shall be connected at the floor end by a pair of longitudinal and a pair of transverse angles. The upright members shall support a formed metal top with a perineal cut -out. The arrangement for welding the sheet metal tops and the upright member shall be sturdy and sound. The perineal cut -out side of the table shall have arrangement for receiving two lithotomy rods which shall be designed to provide rigid support. The table shall be free from burrs and sharp edges. The floor ends of the uprights shall be fitted with aluminium shoes. Additionally, a drainage pipe shall be provided. The top of the table shall have a slope to facilitate drainage into the drain hole. 7 TESTING REQUIREMENTS 7.1 Adhesion Test The adhesion test required for the table shall conform to 6.1.1 of IS 4033. 8 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH The finish for the table shall be in accordance with 7 of IS 4033. 9 MARKING 9.1 The marking which is used by the manufacturer shall be legibly and indelibly marked with the Identification mark of the manufacturer. 9.2 BIS Certification Marking The product(s) conforming to the requirements of this standard may be certified as per the conformity assessment schemes under the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules and Regulations framed thereunder, and the product(s) may be marked with the Standard Mark. 10 PACKAGING The table shall be packed as agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer. chunks.text: Doc: MHD 12 (34171) WC July 2026 1 1 SCOPE This standard specifies the manually controlled hydraulic Albee’s type orthopaedic operation table. 2 REFERENCES The standards given below contain provisions which, through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision, and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of these standards. IS No. Title IS 6911: 2026 Stainless Steel Plate, Sheet and Strip - Specification ( third revision) IS 1068: 2025 ISO 1456: 2009 Metallic and other inorganic coatings - Electrodeposited coatings of nickel, nickel plus chromium, copper plus nickel and of copper plus nickel plus chromium (fourth revision) IS 17523: 2021 Castors and Wheels - Requirements for Castors for Furniture 3 MATERIAL REQUIREMENTS 3.1 The materials used for the manufacturing of the operating table shall be corrosion-resistant or shall have a protective coating. 3.2 The raising column and the gearing system shall be made from wear-resistant material. 3.3 The knobs shall be made from ebonite or plastics that withstand mild acids. 3.4 The stainless steel used for the operation table shall conform to designation X07Cr17Ni12Mo2 in accordance with IS 6911. 3.5 The anti-static rubber tread castors shall conform to IS 17523. 4 SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS 4.1 The shape of the operation table shall be as shown in Fig. 1. 4.2 Length and Width The overall length of the table top including the leg section shall be 1800±50 mm. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. IS No. Title IS 6911: 2026 Stainless Steel Plate, Sheet and Strip - Specification ( third revision) IS 17523: 2021 Castors and Wheels - Requirements for Castors for Furniture IS 1068: 2025 ISO 1456: 2009 Metallic and other inorganic coatings - Electrodeposited coatings of nickel, nickel plus chromium, copper plus nickel and of copper plus nickel plus chromium (fourth revision) 3 TERMINOLOGY 3.1 Paediatric Operation Table - The specialized surgical table designed to support and position infant, child, and adolescent patients safely and comfortably during surgical procedures. 4 MATERIAL REQUIREMENTS 4.1 The materials used for the manufacture of the operation table shall be either corrosion - resistant or have a protective finish. 4.2 The raising column and the gearing system shall be made from materials that are wear - resistant during normal manipulation. 4.3 The handles provided shall be made from ebonite or plastics that can stand the action of mild acids. 4.4 The stainless-steel components used shall conform to designation X07Cr17Ni12Mo2 in accordance with IS 6911. 4.5 The anti-static rubber tread castors shall conform to IS 17523. 5 SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS 5.1 The shape of the operation table shall be as shown in Fig. 1 5.2 Table Top The minimum overall length of the table top shall be 1500 mm. chunks.title: Paediatric Operation Table - Specification (First Revision)

chunks.text: Doc: MHD 12 (34172) WC July 2026 2 6 CONSTRUCTION REQUIREMENTS 6.1 Base The base shall be mounted on castors in such a way that it shall not render the operation table unstable. The base may have foot rails for providing comfortable foot rest to the surgical team. The base shall be fitted with a foot pedal to raise and lower the table top. 6.2 Table Top The table top shall have minimum four sections that are head, trunk (two sections) and leg section. The head section shall be detachable. The detachable assembly of the leg section shall be optional. The entire table top shall have a smooth vertical movement. The table top shall satisfy the following requirements: a) The entire table top shall be capable of being tilted to 45 ±3o Trendelenburg and reverse Trendelenburg positions; b) The table top shall have arrangements for a lateral tilt of 20±2o in either direction; c) The table top may be provided with a perineal cut-out for drainage tray; d) The table top shall be able to obtain kidney position. If the position is not approachable, a separate kidney elevator shall be provided, which is capable of being raised to 150 mm from the table top and shall have a head-end control for manipulation; e) The entire table top may have a sweep of 360o in the horizontal plane; f) The upper half of the trunk section with the head section shall be capable of being raised to 90o and lowered to 30o. 6.2.1 Head and Leg Sections The head section shall be capable of being raised to 40 to 45 o and in reverse position 90o from the trunk portion. The leg section shall be capable of being lowered to at least 90 o from the trunk to enable the table to be used as a chair and also for obtaining other positions. 6.3 Hydraulic Lifting Mechanism The table shall have a hydraulic pump encased in the base for controlling the lift of the table and the pump shall be operated by a pedal. The table shall be lifted between 200 and 300 mm. The controls shall have easy access and various parts of the controls and the table shall be easy to clean and maintain. The parts intended to be removed by the user shall be easy to replace. Fig. 1 PAEDIATRIC OPERATION TABLE

chunks.text: Doc: MHD 12 (34174) WC July 2026 1 1 SCOPE This standard specifies the construction and performance requirements of manually controlled folding type operation table. 2 REFERENCES The standards given below contain provisions which, through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision, and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of these standards. IS No. Title MHD 12 (33411) WC (Under Development) General requirements for hospital furniture (first revision) IS 6911: 2026 Stainless Steel Plate, Sheet and Strip - Specification ( third revision) IS 1068: 2025 ISO 1456: 2009 Metallic and other inorganic coatings - Electrodeposited coatings of nickel, nickel plus chromium, copper plus nickel and of copper plus nickel plus chromium (fourth revision) 3 MATERIAL REQUIREMENTS 3.1 Angles, Flats, Strips and Rods The components shall be made up of mild steel with cold rolled or hot rolled quality. 3.2 Top The top shall be made up of aluminium alloy with suitable composition or stainless-steel conforming to designation X07Cr18Ni9S given in Table 1 of IS 6911 or mild steel sheet with hot rolled or cold rolled quality. 4 DIMENSIONS 4.1 The dimensions of various parts present in operation table shall be as per given below: Component Dimensions Head Section 300 x 500 mm Trunk Section 1050 x 500 mm Leg Section 450 x 500 mm Gap between sections 10 mm Height from floor to top of table 850 mm 4.2 The tolerance of ± 5 mm shall be allowed on all parts of the operation table except Gap between sections, the tolerance for Gap between sections shall be ± 2 mm.

chunks.text: Doc: MHD 12 (34174) WC July 2026 2 5 CONSTRUCTION REQUIREMENTS 5.1 Framework The framework of continuous lengths of mild steel tubes shall be welded to give the desired shape. The floor ends of the tubular framework shall be fitted with metal shoes with rounded edges. 5.2 Table Top The table top shall have a minimum of three sections that is head, trunk and leg section. The leg section shall be detachable. The entire top shall be capable of satisfying the following requirements: a) The head end shall be capable of being raised by 60o up and 45o down. b) The trunk section shall support the body and be capable of being raised by 45o. 5.3 The lowering and raising of the two sections shall be arranged with a ratchet and hook arrangement. 5.4 The operation table shall have provision to attach optional accessories like anaesthetic screen, saline drip, arm rest, instrument tray and lithotomy rod at hip level. 6 ACCESSORIES The following accessories shall be optional: TABLE 1 LIST OF ACCESSORIES Sr No. Accessories i) Detachable instrument tray ii) Rubber, mattress in three pieces 7 PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS 7.1 Base The construction of the table shall ensure stability of the base. The metal framework shall have four metal shoes to provide sufficient rigidity to the table. 7.2 Table Top The load of 750 N shall be applied on the operation table vertically in the middle of the table from height of 100 mm, when load is applied there shall not be wobble or damage to the table. 8 TESTING REQUIREMENTS 8.1 Adhesion Test The adhesion test required for the operation table shall conform to 6.1.1 of IS 4033. 9 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 9.1 The components of the operation table shall be finished smooth to provide easy movements. 9.2 The construction of the operation table shall be rigid. 9.3 The entire table shall be capable of folding to a small unit. 9.4 The edges of the table shall be well finished and rounded off. 9.5 The three sections comprising the table top in their normal position shall be in one plane. 9.6 The welded joints shall have welds fully penetrating. 9.7 The surface of the operation table shall be painted in accordance with 7.1 of IS 4033. 9.8 The stainless steel table top shall be passivated. 9.9 The Aluminium top shall be anodized. 9.10 The resulting finish shall be hard and

chunks.source_file: MHD 12 (34619) WC_Needle-Free Injection Systems for Medical Use — Requirements and Test Methods.pdf
chunks.text: Doc: MHD 12 (34619) WC August 2026 NATIONAL ANNEX A (National Foreword) A-1 BIS CERTIFICATION MARKING The product(s) conforming to the requirements of this standard may be certified as per the conformity assessment schemes under the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules and Regulations framed thereunder, and the product(s) may be marked with the Standard Mark. Scope This document applies to safety and performance and testing requirements for single -use and multiple-use Needle-Free Injection Systems ( NFISs) intended for human use in clinics and other medical settings and for personal use by patients. The dose chamber of the NFIS is often disposable and intended to be replaced after either a single use or a limited number of uses. It is sometimes separable from the injection mechanism and often termed a “cartridge”, “ampoule”, “syringe”, “capsule” or “disc”. In contrast, the dose chamber can also incorporate a permanent internal chamber designed to last through the claimed life of the device, and an add itional member or members which eliminate the risk of cross-contamination. Excluded from this document are drug delivery methods which: — involve penetration of a part of the device itself into or through skin or mucous membranes (such as needles, tines, micro-needles, implantable slow-release drug devices); — generate aerosols, droplets, powders or other formulations for inhalation, insufflation, intranasal or oral deposition (such as sprays, inhalers, misters); — deposit liquids, powders, or other substances on the surface of skin or mucosal surfaces for passive diffusion or ingestion into the body (such as transdermal patches, liquid drops); — apply sonic or electromagnetic energy (such as ultrasonic or iontophoretic devices); — infusion systems for adding or metering medication into or through systems of artificial tubes, catheters, and/or needles which themselves enter the body. The technical content of the document has not been enclosed as it is identical with the corresponding ISO standard. For details, please refer to ISO 21649 : 2023 or kindly contact: Head Medical Equipment and Hospital Planning Department 9 Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg New Delhi-110002 Email: mhd@bis.gov.in hmhd@bis.gov.in

Scope This part of ISO 11418 specifies the design, dimensions, material and requirements of tablet glass bottles. Tablet glass bottles are applicable to primary packs used in direct contact with a drug. This part of ISO 11418 is applicable to tablet glass bottles used in pharmacy. Together with the corresponding closure systems, they serve for packaging of pharmaceutical preparations in solid and liquid dosage forms which are not intended for parenteral use. NOTE The potency, purity, stability and safety of a drug during its manufacture and storage can be strongly affected by the nature and performance of the primary pack. chunks.title: Specification and Demonstration of System Reliability of Single-Use Drug Delivery Systems
chunks.source_file: MHD 12 (34622) WC_Specification and Demonstration of System Reliability of Single-Use Drug Delivery Systems.pdf
chunks.text: Doc: MHD 12 (34622) WC August 2026 Scope This document addresses the specification and demonstration of capability and system reliability to successfully deliver a medicinal product as part of design verification and manufacture, utilizing empirical methods as well as modelling. This includes risk -based techniques to establish and demonstrate the required reliability level for all disposable single use drug delivery systems (DDSs) for which there is a single opportunity to deliver a single dose of a medicinal product. DDSs covered by this document include, but are not limited to: — needle-based injection systems (ISO 11608-1); — needle-free injection systems (ISO 21649); — aerosol drug delivery systems (ISO 20072). This document does not cover: — DDSs with containers that can be replaced; — DDSs intended for dental use; — finished needles; — empty syringes; — catheters; — DDSs for multi-patient use; — pumps [IEC 60601-2-24 (if electronic) or ISO 28620 (if non-electronic)]; — stand-alone prefilled syringes defined by ISO 11040-8. In this document system reliability is limited to assessing functional performance of the DDS and does not address human factors or user interface considerations. These will be covered by a usability engineering program in accordance with IEC 62366-1. NOTE DDSs not in scope of this document can still benefit from elements in this document but provisions of this document might not completely fulfil the basic safety and effectiveness of such DDSs. The technical content of the document has not been enclosed as it is identical with the corresponding ISO standard. For details, please refer to ISO/TS 4452 : 2025 or kindly contact: Head Medical Equipment and Hospital Planning Department 9 Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg New Delhi-110002 Email: mhd@bis.gov.in hmhd@bis.gov.in

chunks.text: Doc: MHD 12 (35061) WC August 2026 NATIONAL ANNEX A (National Foreword) A-1 BIS CERTIFICATION MARKING The product(s) conforming to the requirements of this standard may be certified as per the conformity assessment schemes under the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules and Regulations framed thereunder, and the product(s) may be marked with the Standard Mark. Scope This document specifies particular requirements for washer-disinfectors (WD) intended for use when the level of assurance of disinfection that is necessary can be achieved by cleaning and thermal disinfection (A0 not less than 60) and does not require an independent automated record of critical processes to be kept. It is intended to be used in conjunction with ISO 15883- 1, which specifies general requirements for WD. The range of products on which WD of this particular type can be used is restricted to non - invasive and non -critical devices and equipment (i.e. not penetrating skin or contacting mucosal surfaces). NOTE Thermal disinfection can be achieved by rinsing the load with hot water, exposure to steam, or combination of the two. This document does not cover powered devices, lumened devices, and other semi -critical and critical medical devices. Devices identified within the scopes of ISO 15883 -2, ISO 15883 -3, ISO 15883-4, and ISO 15883-7 do not fall within the scope of this document. The technical content of the document has not been enclosed as it is identical with the corresponding ISO standard. For details, please refer to ISO 15883-6 : 2026 or kindly contact: Head Medical Equipment and Hospital Planning Department 9 Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg New Delhi-110002 Email: mhd@bis.gov.in hmhd@bis.gov.in

IS No. Title IS 1068:2025 Metallic and Other Inorganic Coatings — Electrodeposited Coatings of Nickel, Nickel Plus Chromium, Copper Plus Nickel and of Copper Plus Nickel Plus Chromium ( fourth revision ) IS 2102 (Par t 1) : 1993 General Tolerances Part 1 Tolerances for Linear and Angular Dimensions Without Individual Tolerance Indications (third revision) IS 2500 (Part 1) : 2000 Sampling procedures for inspection by attributes: Part 1 sampling schemes indexed by acceptance quality limit (AQL) for lot - By - Lot inspection (third revision) IS 3748 : 2022 Tool Steels — Specification ( third revision ) 3 MATERIAL Shall conform to designation C120U of IS 3748. 4 SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS 4.1 Shall Conform to Fig. 1. 4.2 The tolerance on dimensions of working ends shall conform to ‘fine’ class of deviation and the tolerance for remaining dimensions shall conform to ‘medium’ class of deviation of IS 2102 (Part 1). 5 MANUFACTURE WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 5.1 The chisel shall be manufactured in one piece. chunks.text: Doc: MHD13 (xxxxx) WC July 2026 3 The chisel shall be hardened and tempered to achieve the following hardness: a) Blade — 650 to 700 HV, and b) Handle — 400 to 500 HV. 7 REQUIREMENTS The chisel shall be plated chromium over nickel conforming to service condition number 2 of IS 1068, except bevelled edge which shall be sharpened. 8 TESTS 8.1 Performance Test The cutting edge of the blade of the chisel shall have a piece of hardwood such as Kusum or Bulletwood quickly and cleanly. On completion of the test, the chisel shall not show any sign of damage. 8.2 Load Test The handle of the chisel at a point approximately 25 mm from the proximal end shall be fixed in a vice (with the centre line parallel with the jaws of the vic e). A proof load of 34 kg, Min shall be applied at the proximal end of the handle. On completion of the test, the chisel shall not take a permanent set. 8.3 Corrosion Test 8.3.1 The instrument shall be cleaned with a suitable organic solvent (for example, carbon tetrachloride) in order to remove any trace of grease before carrying out the test. 8.3.2 The instrument shall be boiled for 60 minutes in 5 percent aqueous solution of sodium carbonate. At the end of this period, the plating shall not show any sign of peeling off nor shall there be any rusting over the plated portion. 8.3.3 The instrument shall be placed on a perforated platform on a desiccator above a so lution of sodium chloride (20 gm NaCl in 100 cc of water of specific gravity of 1.50). Air shall be blown into the solution so that a dense fog is produced in the desiccator without being blown directly against the instrument. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision, and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of these standards. IS No. Title IS 2102 (Part 1) : 1993 General Tolerances Part 1 Tolerances for Linear and Angular Dimensions Without Individual Tolerance Indications (third revision) IS 2500 (Part 1) : 2000 Sampling procedures for inspection by attributes: Part 1 sampling schemes indexed by acceptance quality limit (AQL) for lot - By - Lot inspection (third revision) IS 3748 : 2022 Tool Steels – Specification ( Third Revision ) 3 MATERIAL Shall conform to designation C120U of IS 3748. 4 SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS 4.1 Shall Conform to Fig. 1. 4.2 The tolerance on dimensions of working ends shall conform to ‘fine’ class of deviation and the tolerance for remaining dimensions shall conform to ‘medium’ class of deviation of IS 2102 (Part 1). 5 MANUFACTURE WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 5.1 The surfaces of the rasps except for the tines and threads shall be smooth and free from pitting. The edges shall be even and rounded. The tines shall be well formed. The form and pitch of the threads shall be correct. The male part of rasp shall screw accurately into the female parts of rasp. The male rasp of one set shall fit accurately into the female rasps of any other set in the same supply and vice versa. 5.2 The surface of the working ends shall be free from all defects like burrs, pits, cracks, nicks and waviness when examined under x 10 magnification. All surfaces shall be free from pores, crevices and grinding marks. 5.3 The rasps shall be supplied free from residual scales, acid, grease and grinding and polishing materials. Compliance with these requirements shall be checked under x 2 magnification. 6 HARDNESS Rasp shall be accurately and evenly hardened and tempered to give a hardness of 650 to 750 HV. 7 TESTS

chunks.text: Doc: MHD13 (34605) WC July 2026 3 Each rasp piece shall be used for filing the teeth on a horse jaw bone continuously for two minutes. The rasp shall be able to do it easily. On completion of the test, the tines on the rasp shall not show any sign of wear. 8 SURFACE FINISH The surface finish shall be mirror finish. The instrument should be adequately ground to remove all surface imperfections and pol ished to remove grinding marks, resulting in a mirror finish. The mirror finish should be effected by an appropriate procedure, such as polishing, brushing, electroplolishing and mirror buffing. 9 SAMPLING 9.1 Unless otherwise agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier, the sampling procedure given in IS 2500 (Part 1) shall be followed. 9.2 Lot All tooth rasps of the same size, shape and belonging to the same batch of manufacture shall be grouped together to constitute a lot. 9.3 For dimensions and requirements given in 4, 5 and 8. a single sampling plan with general inspection level II and AQL 4 percent given in Tables 1 and 2-A of IS 2500 (Part 1) shall be followed. 9.4 For the requirement given in 6, a single sampling plan with special inspection level S-3 and AQL 1 percent given in Tables 1 and 2-A of IS 2500 (Part 1) shall be followed. 10 MARKING 10.1 Each rasp shall be legibly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer’s n ame, initials or recognized trademarks. 10.2 BIS Certification Marking The product(s) confirming to the requirements of this standard may be certified as per the conformity assessment schemes under the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules and Regulations framed thereunder, and the product(s) may be marked with the Standard Mark. 11 PACKING The set of rasps shall be delivered in a new an d clean condition free from all traces of rust. Each rasp shall be coated with a thin film of rust preventing solution and wrapped in normal waxed grade kraft paper. The rasp shall be packed in a set in leather case and tied with a strap The empty space, if any, shall be filled with suitable cushioning material to prevent movement.

chunks.text: Doc: MHD 17 (34655) WC August 2026 Scope Within the field of health informatics, the DICOM (digital imaging and communication in medicine) standard addresses the exchange of digital images, and information related to the production and management of those images, between both medical imaging equi pment and systems concerned with the management and communication of that information, such as Picture Archiving anc Communication System (PACS), Hospital Information System (HIS) and Radiology Information System (RIS). This document is equivalent to part 1 of DICOM. As such, it normatively describes the content of DICOM and the requirements to make a claim of conformance. It is also applicable to a wide range of image and non -image related information exchanged in clinical, research, veterinary, and other medical environments. chunks.text: Doc: MHD 17 (34657) WC August 2026 Scope This document supports interchangeability of digital signatures and the prevention of incorrect or illegal digital signatures by providing minimum requirements and formats for generating and verifying digital signatures and related certificates. This document describes the common technical, operational, and policy requirements to enable digital certificates to be used in protecting the exchange of healthcare informa tion within a single domain, between domains, and across jurisdictional boundaries. The purpose of this document is to create a platform for global interoperability. It specifically supports digital certificate enabled communication across borders but can also provide guidance for the national or regional deployment of digital certificates in healthcare. This document defines the provable compliance with a public key infrastructure (PKI) policy necessary in the domain of healthcare. It specifies a method o f adopting long-term signature formats to ensure integrity and non -repudiation in long -term electronic preservation of healthcare information. This document provides healthcare-specific PKI (HPKI) profiles of digital signature based on the ISO/ETSI standa rd profiles specified in CAdES (CMS Advanced Electronic Signature) , XAdES (XML Advanced Electronic Signature), PAdES (PDF Advanced Electronic Signature) and the ETSI standard specified in JAdES (JSON Advanced Electronic Signature). The technical content of the document has not been enclosed as it is identical with the corresponding I SO Technical Specification. chunks.text: Doc: MHD 17 (34658) WC August 2026 Scope This document defines universal and specialized characteristics of health terminological resources that make them fit for the purposes required of various applications. It covers only terminological resources that are primarily designed to be used for clinical concept representation or to those parts of other terminological resources designed to be used for clinical concept representation. This document helps users to assess whether a terminology has the characteristics or provides the functions that will support their specified requirements. In order to do that, this document focuses on defining characteristics and functions of terminological resources in healthcare that can be used to identify different types of terminological resources for categorization purposes. NOTE 1 Categorization of healthcare terminological systems according to the n ame of the system might not be helpful and has caused confusion in the past. The following aspects are not covered in this document: — evaluations of terminological resources; — health service requirements for terminological resources and evaluation criteria based on the characteristics and functions; — the nature and quality of mappings between different terminologies; NOTE 2 It is unlikely that a single terminology will meet all the terminology requirements of a healthcare organization: some terminology providers produce mappings to administrative or classification systems such as the International Classification of Diseases (ICD). The presence of such maps would be a consideration in the evaluation of the terminology. — the nature and quality of mappings between different versions of the same terminology; NOTE 3 To support data migration and historical retrieval, terminology providers can provide maps between versions of their terminology. The presence of such maps would be a consideration in the evaluation of the terminology. — terminology server requirements and techniques and tools for terminology developers; — characteristics for computational biology terminology. The technical content of the document has not been enclosed as it is identica l with the corresponding I SO Technical Specification.
